reason: Selected statistical and cross-domain results support testing for communication-induced contamination, not claiming proven SSVP superiority over no synchronization.

candidates.title: Test whether shared-state broadcasts spread a wrong belief
candidates.rule: Before broadcasting every agent state to all peers, inject plausible stale or incorrect shared facts and compare no synchronization, full broadcast and selective reconciliation.
candidates.passage: The contamination effect, however, does not replicate
candidates.finding: In travel planning, full broadcast raises the reported hallucination rate from 0.492 to 0.658; selective reconciliation gives 0.463 but is not significantly better than no-sync (p=0.257). In software planning, broadcast and selective reconciliation both score 0.150 versus 0.188 no-sync.
candidates.conditions: Controlled injected mismatches; travel sample sizes 30/30/15 and software 10/10/5. Shared destination errors can cascade through related outputs.
candidates.limitations: Small samples, one model, structured scenarios and asymmetric call budgets. The source has inconsistent overhead arithmetic and should not support precise cost claims without artifact checks. Lower state divergence is not proof of factual correctness.
candidates.validation_test: Seed stale destinations, platforms and requirements; compare output correctness and correction propagation across synchronization policies. Track calls directly and distinguish convergence from truth.
